external_entities.name: duty engineer
external_entities.description: An engineer who uses the dispatch console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.
external_entities.notes: The description uses the plural 'Duty engineers'; this element represents the named actor type.

external_entities.name: scheduling partner
external_entities.description: Another company that publishes tomorrow's planned work.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.

processes.name: corporate web host
processes.description: The host that serves the dispatch console application.
processes.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

processes.name: dispatch console
processes.description: A single-page JavaScript application used by duty engineers.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down how an engineer signs in to it.

processes.name: dispatch API
processes.description: The API called by the dispatch console and schedule importer.
processes.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
processes.notes: The API answers the console cross-origin. CORS origins and credential settings are undocumented.

processes.name: schedule importer
processes.description: An hourly importer that retrieves the scheduling partner's SOAP feed, parses XML, archives the document, and posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The importer presents an API token that was issued when it was built and has not been rotated.

data_stores.name: dispatch database
data_stores.description: Database containing job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: How the database is protected at rest is not written down anywhere.

data_stores.name: schedule archive
data_stores.description: A folder containing each XML document downloaded from the scheduling partner.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive
data_stores.notes: The archive is described as a folder on the corporate file store.

data_stores.name: corporate file store
data_stores.description: The file store on which the schedule archive folder resides.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a folder on the corporate file store
data_stores.notes: The description does not state where the file store runs or how it is protected at rest.

data_flows.name: load console
data_flows.description: The duty engineer loads the dispatch console from the corporate web host.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser. ... our corporate web host serves it.

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: A duty engineer, acting through the console, calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.notes: The description does not state how an engineer signs in to the console.

data_flows.name: live job status
data_flows.description: The dispatch console opens and holds a WebSocket to the dispatch API for live job status.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.notes: The description does not state whether the socket uses TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, or whether it rechecks the engineer's session.

data_flows.name: read-write database
data_flows.description: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order

data_flows.name: pull SOAP feed
data_flows.description: The schedule importer pulls the scheduling partner's planned-work feed.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS
data_flows.notes: Nothing was written down about how the partner identifies the importer or how the importer identifies the partner.
data_flows.data_description: tomorrow's planned work in an XML document

data_flows.name: write schedule archive
data_flows.description: The schedule importer writes each downloaded XML document to the schedule archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.description: The schedule importer posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls.
data_flows.notes: The importer presents an API token. The token was issued when the importer was built and has not been rotated.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where duty engineers sit and the schedule importer runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: The same-company zone holding the live estate and authority to move crews or change depot work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
trust_boundaries.notes: The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: scheduling partner
trust_boundaries.description: The zone controlled by the separate company that publishes planned work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database is confidential because it contains crew names, crew mobile numbers, and token or session values.
assumptions.basis: The description states that the database holds job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.

assumptions.assumption: The schedule archive is confidential because it contains downloaded planned-work documents.
assumptions.basis: The description states that downloaded scheduling documents are written into the archive.

assumptions.assumption: The corporate file store is confidential because it contains the schedule archive folder and its planned-work documents.
assumptions.basis: The description identifies the schedule archive as a folder on the corporate file store.
